title: A NATO ISR adaptation exercise produced flight hours and intelligence products without proving decision effect or public legitimacy
source_unit: NATO Intelligence, Surveillance and Reconnaissance Force account of the 2026 Adaptable Capability Exercise
geography: Finland, Italy, Norway, and NATO operational decision-makers

observations.period: 2026 Adaptable Capability Exercise; official NISRF closeout account

denominator.unit: NISRF Adaptable Capability Exercise operational period

platform_output.unit: approximately flight hours accumulated by NATO-owned RQ-4D Phoenix aircraft

intelligence_products.unit: more than intelligence products produced in support of NATO activities, exercise objectives, and Alliance decision-makers

operational_adaptation.value: NISRF conducted operations from Finland while supporting major NATO activities and maintaining persistent ISR across the exercise

decision_effect.unit: missing product use, decision change, mission outcome, adversary response, and deterrence

observations.method: Bounded extraction from the official NISRF closeout account; aircraft hours, intelligence-product production, host-location adaptation, and downstream decision effect are retained as separate stages.
observations.uncertainty: The account does not identify product content, classification, consumers, quality, timeliness, decision changes, operator workload, Finnish or host costs, civilian burden, adversary response, or the exercise's durable continuation.
observations.subgroup: NISRF personnel, NATO operational staffs, host-nation institutions, and supported activities; no civilian or public-opinion denominator is supplied.
observations.counterinterpretation: Producing products and flying from an alternate location can demonstrate organizational adaptability without proving that information improved decisions, changed external behavior, or generated durable alliance legitimacy.

related_sources.claim: NATO describes NISRF's broader surveillance and intelligence role and its alliance context.
A separate NISRF account reports a Belgian MQ-9B deployment; it is retained as a related but distinct national-capability episode.

boundary: This record establishes NATO ISR output and alternate-location operational adaptation during a named exercise. It does not establish intelligence quality, decision effect, adversary response, deterrence, public consent, host burden, cost sustainability, or durable geopolitical leverage.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: The hash covers the official NISRF closeout-page HTML retrieved for extraction.
